evidence.excerpt:
Construction
Figure 1 illustrates the speech-to-memory pipeline.
For each spoken turn, an audio LLM (Xu et al.,
2025b) generates a transcript, while a speaker-
embedding model extracts acoustic identity evi-
dence. The router (Section 2.2) assigns the turn to
an existing local entity or creates a new one. The
transcript, assigned entity identifier, and timestamp
are then passed to a replaceable text-memory back-
end (Fang et al., 2026), which extracts and indexes
atomic facts within the corresponding user's mem-
ory partition. Each entity thus maintains acoustic
state and user-attributed textual memory, while tran-
script semantics do not influence acoustic routing
or center updates.
At query time, read-only voice matching against
the registry identifies the relevant entity and re-
stricts retrieval to its memory partition; unmatched
requests receive no personal memory. The same

We evaluate online speaker-memory construction
using a causal first-seen binding protocol. When a
local entity is first created, it is bound to the gold
speaker of that turn only for post-hoc scoring. The
6https://anonymous.4open.science/r/
EvoSpeakerMem-4AF1
binding is immutable and never affects routing, up-
dating, or memory construction; a later assignment
is correct only when it matches this binding. This
avoids future-aware cluster matching, which could
relabel entities after observing the full sequence
and hide online routing errors.
Each turn is categorized into one of five mutually
exclusive routing outcomes: new-speaker creation,
new-speaker linking, known-speaker creation, cor-
rect known-speaker linking, and wrong-target link-
ing. These outcomes capture two complementary
failure modes of online entity maintenance: frag-
mentation, where a known speaker is assigned to
a new

evidence.excerpt:
Our evaluation has several limitations. LoCoMo-
ID uses synthetic voices; shifted-condition sim-
ulates session-dependent rooms, microphones,
device chains, and noise rather than naturally
recorded, overlapping multi-user conversations.
The standard clean and shifted-condition collec-
tions each contain two participants. Our four-

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Ground-truth speaker bindings and reference-answer judgments provide evaluator-independent measurement of the reported gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by causal first-seen binding against gold speaker identities, objective routing metrics such as B3 F1 and FNUR, and downstream QA judged against reference answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system's routing and update thresholds are fixed at domain-calibrated EER operating points on reference voice banks, and the maintenance policies are training-free; no learned evaluator or model-generated score is optimized against the reported outcomes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the degradation of fixed voiceprint templates over time and the superiority of gated acoustic updating over static representations are directly supported by the data (e.g., Table 4 and Table 5). The authors candidly highlight the fragmentation–contamination trade-off, showing how certain updating policies improve QA while occasionally increasing wrong-user authorizations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation thoroughly validates the approach across longitudinal real-speaker verification (SMIIP-TV) and the synthetic multi-session LoCoMo-ID benchmark with clean, condition-shifted, and four-speaker interleaved settings. Metrics clearly separate routing accuracy (B3 F1, FNUR, linking precision) from downstream authorization outcomes (C/W/D) and end-to-end question answering.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation relies on causal ground-truth speaker identity bindings and objective reference-answer match judgments via standard LoCoMo QA benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Causal online clustering metrics (B3 F1, FNUR) against ground-truth speaker labels, downstream Top-1 authorization correctness, and LLM-as-a-judge QA evaluation against reference ground truth.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Thresholds (tau_merge and tau_update) are fixed based on domain-calibrated EER operating points on reference voice banks without learned parameter optimization.

primary.limitations: The manuscript comprehensively documents limitations, noting that LoCoMo-ID uses synthetic voices rather than spontaneous overlapping multi-party recordings, that condition shifts rely on acoustic simulations, and that the identity-gated access protocol serves as an experimental proxy rather than a production biometric security system.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described in detail, specifying the causal first-seen binding protocol, cosine similarity scoring with calibrated thresholds (tau_merge and tau_update), and the integration with a replaceable text memory backend (LightMem). Controls across baseline policies (Fixed, Update, Gated Update, and All-exemplar KNN) and alternative acoustic frontends (ECAPA-TDNN vs ReDimNet2-B6; per-turn vs diarization) are soundly executed.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-motivated, and novel framing of speaker attribution in conversational memory, accompanied by extensive empirical analysis across real longitudinal datasets and realistic conversational stress tests. The experiments are methodologically transparent and properly controlled.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formulates online speaker-memory construction for multi-user conversational agents, proposing EvoSpeakerMem (a training-free speech support layer separating speaker routing from selective acoustic updates) and introducing LoCoMo-ID to benchmark speaker-sensitive memory retrieval and question answering under acoustic drift.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-motivated, and novel framing of speaker attribution in conversational memory, accompanied by extensive empirical analysis across real longitudinal datasets and realistic conversational stress tests. The experiments are methodologically transparent and properly controlled.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript comprehensively documents limitations, noting that LoCoMo-ID uses synthetic voices rather than spontaneous overlapping multi-party recordings, that condition shifts rely on acoustic simulations, and that the identity-gated access protocol serves as an experimental proxy rather than a production biometric security system.
